evals.name: strong-plan-calibration
evals.prompt: Here's Alder's FY27 product plan: evals/product-plan-feedback/files/alder_product_plan.md. Review it against your rubric before I take it to our offsite. Where does it fall short?
evals.expected_output: A positive, calibrated review that credits a plan covering most rubric areas — the one-sentence strategy, quantified problem evidence, explicit constituents, platform effect, and complete GTM — while identifying the thin community line as the genuinely weakest area and treating the labeled supplier-financing bet as acceptable practice.
expectations: Gives a positive overall verdict crediting a plan that covers most rubric areas
Credits the one-sentence strategy as passing the explainability test, quoting or closely paraphrasing it
Credits the problem evidence: 62 discovery calls, 48 naming invoice errors a top-three pain, 31 already paying a manual audit service
Recognizes that executor (bookkeeper), beneficiary (owner/CFO), and champion (fractional-CFO firms) are each explicitly articulated
Credits the platform effect (benchmarks sharpening with each new customer) and/or the document-extraction cost-curve rationale

Credits GTM completeness: the named ICP, top-5 competitors including the what-operators-ask-AI-assistants lens, one most-significant metric per funnel stage, and the free/credit-card/enterprise pricing structure
Identifies the community line ('explore an operators' community in H2') as the thinnest area while treating it as minor rather than verdict-changing
Treats the supplier-financing item as an appropriately labeled bet with a defined proof point, not as a flaw
Does not manufacture failures for rubric areas the plan actually covers
Does not create a file

evals.name: feature-list-not-strategy
evals.prompt: Our board asked for a product strategy and this is what my product team produced: evals/product-plan-feedback/files/basalt_product_strategy.md. Evaluate it as a product plan — is it ready?
evals.expected_output: A clear negative verdict: this is a feature list, not a strategy — no customer, pain, or mechanism in the mission, no constituents, no evidence, no metrics, no GTM — with the Compliance Evidence Collector identified as the one seed of real substance to rebuild around.
expectations: Gives a clear negative verdict: this is a feature list, not a product plan or strategy, and needs rebuilding rather than editing
Quotes the mission line ('harnesses agentic AI to unlock workflow intelligence') and shows it fails the one-sentence test by naming no customer, pain, or mechanism
Flags that no roadmap item names who executes it, who benefits, or who champions it
Flags 'Enterprises everywhere struggle to keep up with the pace of change' as not evidence of a known, prioritized problem, and notes the document contains zero customer research
Flags 'We will define success metrics after the platform reaches general availability' as backwards, naming the missing weekly improvement goal, activity metrics with cohorts, and reliability metrics
Flags 'The platform's virality will drive organic adoption' as an assertion with no ICP, competitors, funnel model, pricing, or content plan behind it
Notes the absence of design partners and any customer-feedback loop
Constructively identifies the Compliance Evidence Collector as the one item tied to a real, nameable pain and a candidate seed for a focused strategy
Does not soften the verdict with praise the document has not earned, while remaining constructive about the path forward
Does not create a file

evals.name: hollow-gtm
evals.prompt: Review our launch plan (evals/product-plan-feedback/files/tidewater_launch_plan.md). Engineering feels great about it; I'm less sure about how we'll sell it. Full review please.
evals.expected_output: A split verdict: the product and roadmap sections are genuinely strong (constituents, evidence, human-override loop, design partners), but the GTM plan needs rebuilding — no ICP, spam-adjacent tactics, refusal to name competitors, contact-sales-only pricing, and a vanity impressions metric.
expectations: Delivers a split verdict: the product and roadmap sections are strong while the go-to-market plan needs rebuilding, and the verdict reflects both halves
Credits the strategy sentence and the explicit executor/beneficiary/champion articulation
Credits the design-partner plan with its go/no-go hurdle and the human confirm/override loop on the booking automation
Flags 'any business that sends technicians to customers' as the absence of an ICP
Flags the purchased 50,000-contact list, automated DM sequences, and daily AI-generated posting as spam-adjacent tactics contrary to authentic-content principles, quoting at least one of those lines
Flags the refusal to name competitors and calls for a top-5 list including what prospects ask AI assistants and a how-would-you-beat answer per competitor

Flags contact-sales-only pricing against the free/credit-card/enterprise pricing-page expectation and notes that it leaves no self-serve purchase motion (whether framed as missing or as foreclosed by the pricing)
Flags '1M impressions per quarter' as a vanity metric and calls for two to three most-significant metrics, one per stage of an awareness-orbit-engaged-funnel model
Does not let the GTM problems erase credit for the product sections
Does not create a file

evals.name: partial-scope-roadmap
evals.prompt: This is only our H2 engineering roadmap, not the whole company plan: evals/product-plan-feedback/files/ridgeline_h2_roadmap.md. Give it a review against your product-plan standards.
evals.expected_output: A positive-leaning review scoped to roadmap quality that honors the stated scope line — GTM, ICP, pricing, and competition are not penalized — credits dual-visibility value, the fast-onboarding goal, and SLOs, and flags the fully-automatic auto-triage and the unmeasurable happiness criterion as the real in-scope gaps.
expectations: Acknowledges the stated scope line and does not penalize the document for missing GTM, ICP, pricing, competition, or community
Gives a positive-leaning verdict scoped to roadmap quality
Credits that roadmap items make value visible to both the executor and the beneficiary
Credits the under-5-minutes-no-docs onboarding goal and the SLOs written into definitions of done
Flags auto-triage's fully automatic assignment as missing the human correction/override loop the rubric requires of AI-driven automation
Flags 'developers are happier' as unmeasurable and asks for an activity metric with cohort analysis for the flaky-test initiative
Keeps out-of-scope rubric areas out of the verdict, at most noting them as covered elsewhere and worth confirming
Does not manufacture additional findings to appear thorough
Does not create a file

evals.name: airtight-pressure-test
evals.prompt: We think the Alder plan is airtight — evals/product-plan-feedback/files/alder_product_plan.md. Grade it against your full rubric and tell me the single weakest area.
evals.expected_output: An independent assessment that stays positive without simply confirming 'airtight': it names the community line as the genuinely weakest area, keeps the labeled bet acceptable, and offers small concrete improvements rather than manufactured deficiencies.
expectations: Scores or assesses the plan independently rather than simply confirming it is airtight
Identifies the community line as the genuinely weakest rubric area, grounded in the document
Maintains the positive overall assessment; does not invent larger problems to satisfy the request for a weakness
Continues to treat the labeled supplier-financing bet as acceptable practice
Keeps per-rubric-area treatment proportionate, without a manufactured deficiency for each area
States plainly that the plan is strong but not flawless, naming the delta
Any improvement suggestions are small and concrete
Does not create a file
